Ideal weight by height: calculator and chart for women and men

Your ideal weight by height is the weight range the WHO considers healthy. A range, not a magic number.

Updated: 8 November 2026 · By Fotocal, Madrid · How we calculate

For guidance only; not a substitute for a health professional. Not for under-18s, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if you have had an eating disorder.

Quick answer: Your healthy weight is a range, not a number: the one that gives a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 by WHO bands. At 1.60 m it runs from 47 to 64 kg; at 1.70 m, from 53 to 72 kg; at 1.80 m, from 60 to 81 kg. Within the range, what is best for you depends on your muscle and build.

How it is calculated

From the body mass index: the World Health Organization considers a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 normal weight for adults. Solving for weight:

lowest = 18.5 × height (m)²  ·  highest = 24.9 × height (m)²

Rounded to the kilo, as the Fotocal app does when it suggests a target weight. If you enter your current weight, the calculator gives your BMI and how many kilos you are from the range, if you are outside it.

A worked example

At 1.70 m: 18.5 × 2.89 = 53 kg and 24.9 × 2.89 = 72 kg. At 1.60 m, 47 to 64 kg; at 1.80 m, 60 to 81 kg. Someone of 1.70 m and 80 kg has a BMI of 27.7 and is 8 kg from the top of the range, not from an "ideal weight" in the low sixties.

Why a range and not an ideal weight

"Ideal weight" formulas (Lorentz, Devine, Broca…) give a single number with no more basis than the range, and it is usually lower than it needs to be. Within those 19 or 20 kilos, what is best for you depends on your muscle, build and history; outside, BMI is not a diagnosis either, for the reasons the BMI calculator explains.

What to do with this number

If you are above it, a reasonable first goal is the top of the range, or losing 5-10% of your weight, which already improves health. Work out your deficit with that goal and it will tell you how long it takes at a sensible pace. Spanish dishes that help without giving up good food: Galician-style octopus, gazpacho, lentil stew (pages in Spanish). If you are below it, talk to a health professional before changing your diet.

Ideal weight by height chart

The weight that gives a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9, from 1.50 to 1.95 m. The third column is the middle of the range (BMI 21.7), in case you want a single reference figure: it is not a target.

Ideal weight for women and for men

The WHO uses the same BMI range for adult women and men, so the chart works for both. What differs is where each tends to sit inside the range: at the same height, a man carries more muscle on average and weighs more at the same body fat. That is why a woman of 1.65 m is often comfortable in the lower half of her range (50 to 68 kg) and a man of 1.80 m in the upper half of his (60 to 81 kg).

Does ideal weight change with age?

The WHO range is for adults of any age. It does not apply to under-18s, who are assessed with growth charts by age and sex, or during pregnancy. From 65 on, many geriatricians prefer a slightly higher BMI; ask your doctor.

Frequently asked questions

What is my ideal weight for my height?

There is no single ideal weight: there is a healthy range, the one that gives a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9. At 1.65 m it runs from 50 to 68 kg. Within it, what is best for you depends on your muscle and build.

Does it work if I am very muscular?

Less well. With a lot of muscle you can be above the range with little fat. Waist size or a body composition measurement say more.

What about over 65?

The cut-offs are debated: a slightly higher BMI, up to 27, is not linked to worse health in older people. Talk to your doctor before setting out to lose weight.

How long would it take to reach the range?

It depends on how many kilos and the pace: at half a kilo a week, 8 kg is about 16 weeks. The calorie deficit calculator works it out with your numbers.
